# Lesson 11: FDTD — Time-Domain, Dispersive Materials, PML

> **Status:** Planned — outline only. See [`dev/plans.md`](../../dev/plans.md#lesson-11--fdtd--time-domain-dispersive-materials-pml).

## Learning Objectives

- Derive the Yee staggered grid placement of $\vec E$ and $\vec H$
- Implement leapfrog update equations in 1D, 2D, and 3D
- Treat dispersive materials (Drude, Debye, Lorentz) via auxiliary-differential-equation (ADE) updates
- Inject plane waves cleanly via the total-field/scattered-field (TF/SF) formulation
- Implement a split-field PML and quantify its reflection coefficient
- Recognize the CFL stability limit and the numerical-dispersion error

## Background

Lessons 01–10. In particular Lesson 04 (material maps), Lesson 09 (plane waves), and Lesson 10 (FDFD — shares the Yee grid and PML ideas).

## Lesson Body

_To be written. When drafted, the body uses one H2 per concept, each split into `### Theory` (prose + math) and one or more `### Example — <descriptor>` (rustlab block paralleling a script below). See [Lesson 01](01-vector-calculus-and-fields.md) for the pattern._

Key equations: 1D Yee updates for $H_y$ and $E_z$ in a medium with $\varepsilon(x)$, $\mu(x)$; CFL $c\Delta t \le \Delta x/\sqrt d$; Drude dispersion $\varepsilon(\omega) = \varepsilon_\infty - \omega_p^2/(\omega^2 + i\gamma\omega)$ via auxiliary polarization current; Berenger split-field PML.
